newsitem.title: UK: Jet jobs boost for N.Ireland's Shorts.
newsitem.headline: Jet jobs boost for N.Ireland's Shorts.

text.p: Shorts, the Northern Ireland aerospace firm, said on Wednesday that design and component work for a new jet, announced by parent company Bombardier, of Canada, would mean up to 600 new jobs at its Belfast plant.

Ken Brundle, Shorts vice-president, said the award of work on the new 70-seat Canadair Regional jet, was "excellent news" after the loss of around 1000 jobs last year when a major contract disappeared with the collapse of Dutch planemaker Fokker.
"We are talking about 500 to 600 jobs, mostly new jobs that will be generated in Belfast over the next three to four years," Brundle told BBC radio.
Bombardier said that Shorts would be responsible for the forward and centre fusilage on the jet, which should be operating by the end of the decade.

Some workers made redundant when the Fokker contract collapsed would "inevitably...be returning, and there will be opportunities for people who have never worked for the company to join as well," Brundle said.
